writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 186 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument. In a world where people come from diverse backgrounds, disagreements are inevitable; yet how we handle them reveals our maturity. Rather than shouting others down or stubbornly clinging to our own views, seeking common ground through calm reasoning is always the wiser choice.
The reason is simple: friendly discussion invites cooperation, while quarrels only deepen the divide. Take the famous debates in scientific communities. When Darwin proposed his theory of evolution, opponents raised sharp objections, but progress was made not by insults but by patient argument and shared evidence. Similarly, in my own study group, a heated dispute over a project was resolved only after we sat down, listened to one another, and combined our ideas. Mutual respect turned rivals into partners.
In conclusion, differing opinions need not lead to conflict. If we approach them with an open mind, sound logic, and genuine respect, we can transform disagreement into understanding and reach a consensus that benefits everyone. This is not only a skill but a mark of a civilized society.

lines.en: M: Have you decided what you wish to study?
lines.zh: M: 你决定想学什么了吗？

lines.en: W: Yes, professor. I wish to study architecture.
lines.zh: W: 是的，教授。我想学习建筑学。

lines.en: M: Ah, that's a wonderful profession. Why did you choose it?
lines.zh: M: 啊，那是一门很棒的职业。你为什么选择它？

lines.en: W: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me. In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
lines.zh: W: 我认真思考了您在上次讨论中说的话，最后决定建筑学对我来说最合适。尤其是，我很喜欢设计与工程的结合。

lines.en: M: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics. You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
lines.zh: M: 这很好，不过我记得你之前一直在担心那些高深的数学。你现在不再觉得这方面对你来说太难了吗？

lines.en: W: No. I was doing some online research and I think I should be able to manage. Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. I'm certain the fruits of my labor will pay off.
lines.zh: W: 不会。我做了一些网上调查，我觉得自己应该能够应付。数学可能是我在课程中遇到的最难的科目，但我会投入所需的努力。我相信我的劳动成果一定会得到回报。

lines.en: M: I'm sure that's true. Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you will be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city. And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
lines.zh: M: 我相信确实如此。由于建筑具有实体性，在这个领域，你将能够清楚地看到自己为一座城市所作出的贡献。而且你所建造的遗产将比我们这些凡人中的任何一个存在得都久远。

lines.en: W: Yeah, I guess that's true too. So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation? I have the whole summer.
lines.zh: W: 嗯，我想这也是真的。那么，为了做准备，您觉得我应该先复习哪些科目？我整个夏天都有时间。

lines.en: M: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree. Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics. Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
lines.zh: M: 如今，建筑学是一门非常多样且充满活力的学位专业。大多数大学都会鼓励你学习来自哲学、经济学等广泛领域的不同知识。不过，我建议你先从计算机科学开始，因为作为项目的一部分，你将需要制作许多复杂的视觉图像。

lines.en: W: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
lines.zh: W: 您觉得我应该先从哪种软件开始，具体来说？

lines.en: M: Photoshop is a good place. If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it. And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art.
lines.zh: M: Photoshop 是个不错的起点。如果你还不熟悉它，就尽量熟练掌握。另外，我建议你尽可能多学习的一项内容是美术，尤其是西方艺术史。

lines.en: W: Good. As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office. So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous. Nothing could be further from the truth. I'm telling you this so that you don't get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you.
lines.zh: W: 很好。作为他的私人助理，你需要替桑切斯先生处理日常琐事，也就是那些由于他的名气而无法亲自去做的事情，比如去超市或邮局。所以，乍一看，为名人工作似乎很光鲜。但事实远非如此。我告诉你这些，是为了让你不要对这份工作能给你带来什么抱有不切实际的期待。

lines.en: M: Thanks. I understand this too. This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience. I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.
lines.zh: M: 谢谢。我对此也很清楚。这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。所以坦白说，我之前没有多少工作经验。不过，我非常期待有机会加入这家公司，也很愿意从基层做起，无论在哪个岗位上，只要我能发挥作用就行。

lines.en: W: That's good to hear. You sound very energetic. Tell me why you think you are well suited for this job?

lines.en: M: Well, firstly, I love football. I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can. I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary. And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool. And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.
lines.zh: M: 首先，我热爱足球。我是皇家马德里的终身支持者，只要有可能，我每个周末都会去看他们的比赛。我非常希望能找一份以某种方式参与皇家马德里事务的工作，不管职位和薪水如何。其次，我觉得这家公司在体育咨询方面所做的事情非常酷。我还认为，我的语言能力将来可能会派上很大用场。

lines.en: Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids. Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal. They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
lines.zh: 冒险运动对许多精力充沛、寻求刺激的孩子来说无疑很有吸引力。因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车等运动颇受欢迎。它们没有传统团队运动中那么多的规则和压力，但仍具备户外体育活动的全部益处。

lines.en: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life. Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to. Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears. But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice. They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill-seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
lines.zh: 在得到适当监管的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康、均衡生活的一部分。有些冒险运动可能伴随着较高的受伤风险，因此，孩子们必须弄清楚什么时候应该冒险，什么时候不应该冒险。没有任何风险的活动会剥夺孩子们挑战自我、克服恐惧的机会。但在一些人看来，正是这些风险使这类运动成为糟糕的选择。他们认为，极限运动往往会导致严重的伤害，尤其是年轻的冒险者可能会尝试对他们来说难度过高的动作。

lines.en: But let's be real. Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not. Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children. As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids. But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives. Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
lines.zh: 但我们还是面对现实吧。不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会做各种各样的危险事情。冒险运动也有许多相同的风险和危险，但它们还具有一种额外的冒险精神、勇气和自主意识，而这些品质对年幼的孩子来说很重要，需要加以培养。一如既往，父母应当决定什么对自己的孩子最好。但如果你确实认为冒险运动有些过于激烈，那就应该努力将其他形式的户外探险引入孩子的生活。在星空下露营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能大大帮助孩子培养与冒险运动相同的自信心和冒险精神。

lines.en: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow. Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing. In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
lines.zh: 今天光鲜亮丽的电子产品明天就会成为废品。当制造商宣布要推出替代你那几乎同样好用的旧产品的新款重磅产品时，他们很少提及这一点。事实上，科技公司往往故意设计使用寿命不长且无法维修的设备，以便消费者不得不花钱购买新设备。

lines.en: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score. If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets. Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
lines.zh: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技制造商标注可维修性评分。如果一台设备可以维修，其使用寿命就能延长，从而为消费者节省资金，并减轻大量报废电子设备给地球带来的负担。掌握了这一信息，消费者在决定购买哪些产品时就能做出更好的选择。

lines.en: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year. This waste is dangerous. Batteries explode in recycling facilities. Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air. Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem. If they won't, governments must make them do so.
lines.zh: 每年约有5900万吨旧电视、电脑、显示屏、智能手机、洗衣机和其他电子产品被废弃。这种废弃物是危险的。电池会在回收设施中发生爆炸。汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并散播到空气中。制造平板显示屏会向大气中排放额外的温室气体。我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。如果他们不愿意，政府就必须强制他们这样做。

lines.en: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits. Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies. Consumers should support right-to-repair legislation. In this world, damage is a certainty. But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
lines.zh: 尽管科技公司经常谈论环境可持续性，但许多公司却游说反对维修立法，担心这会侵蚀它们的利润。可持续性固然重要，但对这些公司而言，具有市场吸引力的设计似乎更为重要。消费者应当支持“维修权”立法。在这个世界上，损坏是必然会发生的。但我们不能任由东西坏着不管：我们制造出的问题是一个可以被解决的问题。

lines.en: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online. This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
lines.zh: 平均而言，美国工人每天约有10%的工作时间用于浏览互联网、给朋友发电子邮件或在线购物。这种被称为“网络闲逛”的行为，据认为每年会因生产力损失而使雇主损失高达850亿美元。

lines.en: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies. But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time. Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction. New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
lines.zh: 大多数关于网络闲逛的研究都集中于如何通过互联网监控和计算机使用政策等干预措施，防止员工从事这种行为。但事实证明，这类行为未必意味着员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间。研究表明，在工作中使用社交媒体与更高水平的员工敬业度和工作满意度相关。新的研究显示，网络闲逛可以帮助员工应对压力异常大的工作环境。

lines.en: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels? That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study. Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations. To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping. We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at. As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit. More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection. That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much. This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
lines.zh: 但网络闲逛是否真的能有效降低员工的压力水平？这正是我的研究团队希望在新研究中回答的问题。我们的假设是，网络闲逛可以起到短暂休息的作用，为员工提供从压力大的工作情境中恢复的机会。为了验证这一点，我们要求员工完成一份在线调查，并对自己花在网络闲逛、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间进行排序。我们还要求他们对工作满意度、离职意愿，以及在工作中遭受不当对待的频率进行评定，例如受到欺凌、威胁或吼叫。正如你所料，我们发现总体而言，工作中遭受的不当对待越多，工作满意度越低，离职意愿越强。更有意思的是，我们发现网络闲逛有效地缓冲了这种关联。也就是说，与网络闲逛较少的类似参与者相比，遭受不当对待但花更多时间浏览网页和查看电子邮件的员工报告了更高的工作满意度，也不太可能想要离职。这表明，网络闲逛对员工而言就像一种减压阀，帮助他们从压力经历中恢复过来。

lines.en: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity. This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance. That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good. Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer. All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees. We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
lines.zh: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络闲逛如何影响员工的工作表现，但我们认为，通过缓解压力，它不仅可能减少员工流失，最终还可能提高生产力。这与其他近期研究的结果相符，即进行短暂休息与更高水平的日常工作表现相关。这并不是说网络闲逛总是有益的。花费过多时间从事非工作活动很可能会导致工作表现下降。总的来说，管理者应该对员工更加宽容。我们认为，在工作中进行一些在线购物或浏览互联网，从长远来看可能会让员工更具生产力。

lines.en: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain. That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel. But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, "For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed". So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land. By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees. A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
lines.zh: 1854年，朱利叶斯·莫顿迁居内布拉斯加城时，面临着该地区许多定居者共同面对的问题：这里是一片没有树木的平原。这意味着没有树木可用作建筑材料，也没有木材可作燃料。但莫顿是世界上最早的自然资源保护主义者之一，他说：“为了繁荣，我们应当种植与已经耗尽和消耗掉的森林一样多的森林。”于是，他开始植树，先从自己的土地种起。到1860年，莫顿已经拥有一片由300多棵树组成的树林。几年后，他拥有的树木超过了1,000棵。

lines.en: As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska. This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting. He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture. While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
lines.zh: 随着树林不断生长，莫顿在内布拉斯加州的影响力也日益扩大。这主要是因为莫顿创办了《内布拉斯加城新闻报》，这是该州的第一份报纸；他经常在报纸上撰写社论，介绍植树在实用和审美方面的益处。他还组织成立了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并担任内布拉斯加州农业委员会委员。任职期间，莫顿想出了一个办法，要将他关于植树的信念传播到全州。

lines.en: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves. Morton called the special event Arbor Day as "arbor" is Latin for "tree". The state government agreed. And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska. Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees. That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska—an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state. Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname "the Tree Planters State".
lines.zh: 1872年1月4日，莫顿起草了一项决议，提议将4月10日定为内布拉斯加州植树日，并号召人们走出家门，亲自植树。莫顿把这一特别活动称为“植树节”，因为“arbor”在拉丁语中意为“树”。州政府同意了这一提议。1872年4月10日，内布拉斯加州各地庆祝了第一个非正式的植树节。植树数量最多的县、市和个人获得了奖励。那一天，内布拉斯加州种下了惊人的100万棵树，平均每位州内居民，包括男女老幼在内，种下了六棵以上的树。自1885年以来，内布拉斯加州已经种植了超过70万英亩的树木，因此获得了“植树州”的昵称。

lines.en: Arbor Day became a legal, civic holiday in the state in 1885. It was held on April 22—Julius Morton's birthday. In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition: School children went outside and planted trees together.
lines.zh: 1885年，植树节在该州成为法定的公民节日。节日定于4月22日举行，这一天是朱利叶斯·莫顿的生日。除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行外，莫顿还引入了一项后来成为植树节长期传统的活动：学生们走到户外，一起植树。

lines.en: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day. All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional state Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
lines.zh: 1970年，也就是植树节首次庆祝近一个世纪后，理查德·尼克松总统宣布将每年4月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。美国50个州都承认在4月举行的这一节日，尽管许多州还会在更适合当地植树的月份另行庆祝本州植树节。

lines.en: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
lines.zh: 现代人类在大约20万年前起源于非洲。随后，他们在距今6万年后的某个时间扩散到了欧洲和亚洲。这就是人们通常所说的“走出非洲”模型。在20世纪90年代，这一假设得到了广泛接受。但鉴于过去几十年间在整个亚洲取得的一系列重要发现，这一流行观点有必要进行修改。

lines.en: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years. This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago. Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
lines.zh: 例如，许多新发现的人类化石（特别是在中国发现的）现在的测年结果都早于6万年前。这使人们对现代人类仅在6万年前才迁出非洲的观点提出了质疑。以最近在中国广西壮族自治区陆那洞发现的两颗现代人类牙齿为例。当我和我的研究团队对这两颗牙齿进行测年时，我们发现它们有超过7万年的历史——如果现代人类仅在6万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然是不可能的。

lines.en: So with such findings, what happened exactly? Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
lines.zh: 那么，面对这些发现，究竟发生了什么？最新的数据表明我们来自何方？

lines.en: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
lines.zh: 我们首先应该问的问题是：现代人类最初为什么离开非洲？如果一个群体完全适应了特定环境并且拥有丰富的资源，那么确实没有理由迁移或改变。例如，非洲的一些猴子的牙齿在数百万年间几乎没有任何变化，这表明它们找到了适合自己的生存之地。

lines.en: So what happened with humans? Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands. Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures. Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
lines.zh: 那么人类发生了什么？一些研究人员提出，人口密度增加到了迫使较小的人类群体不得不去探索新土地的程度。另一些研究人员则认为，由于东非发生的重大环境事件，促使人类去寻找更适宜生存的环境。还有一种解释可能仅仅是，早期的现代人类猎人跟随着他们所依赖的大型动物，因此在没有意识到自己实际上正在从一个大洲迁移到另一个大洲的情况下就移出了非洲。

lines.en: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas. This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa? No clear route across the Mediterranean from North Africa appears to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
lines.zh: 人类每天都需要获得可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎缺乏淡水。这就带出了另一个问题：现代人类是通过哪条路线迁出非洲的？从北非穿过地中海的路线似乎并不存在明确的路径，因此早期走出非洲进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散可能是穿过了阿拉伯半岛。

questions.stem: 【题目】 Why do new tech products soon become waste?

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the speaker say happened on April 10, 1872?
questions.stem_zh: 说话者说1872年4月10日发生了什么?

analysis.定位: P3 And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska. Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees. That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska—an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state. 于是在1872年4月10日，第一个非官方的植树节在内布拉斯加全境举行。奖项颁给了种树最多的县、市和个人。那一天，内布拉斯加种下了惊人的一百万棵树——平均每个男女老少每人种了六棵多。

analysis.替换: an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska↔One million trees were planted throughout Nebraska.去掉修饰即等值

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do we learn about modern humans according to the hypothesis commonly accepted in the 1990s?

analysis.定位: P1 Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. 现代人大约在二十万年前起源于非洲。随后在距今约六万年后的某个时期扩散到欧洲和亚洲。这就是众所周知的『走出非洲』模型。上世纪九十年代，这一假说获得了广泛接受。
analysis.信号: 时间状语锁定旧假说内容。题干限定 in the 1990s 的旧假说，录音里 In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. 把前文 spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago 这段表述归到了那个旧假说名下，因此前面讲迁徙时间的那几句就是答案句。
analysis.替换: spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago↔They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.扩散到欧亚=走出非洲

questions.stem: 【题目】 What has called into question the "Out of Africa" model?
questions.stem_zh: 什么对"走出非洲"模型提出了质疑？

analysis.定位: P2 Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago. 以最近在中国广西壮族自治区娄洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。当我和我的研究团队给这些牙齿测年时，我们发现它们已有七万多年的历史——如果现代人直到六万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然是不可能出现的。
analysis.信号: Take…例子+测年结果证伪旧说。讲者用 Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth 引出一个具体例子，并以 more than 70,000 years old 这个测年结果说明它与旧模型矛盾，正是这个『两颗牙齿』的发现 called into question 了该模型，故定位到这例子。
analysis.替换: the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China↔The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.近乎原句的浓缩

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does the speaker want to show with the example of some monkeys in Africa?
questions.stem_zh: 讲话者想通过非洲某些猴子的例子说明什么？

analysis.定位: P4 The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them. 我们首先该问的是：现代人当初究竟为什么要离开非洲？如果一个种群完美适应了某个特定环境、又能获得充足的资源，那就真的没有理由迁移或改变了。比如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年里几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的栖身之地。

locate.en: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
locate.zh: 我们首先该问的是：现代人当初究竟为什么要离开非洲？如果一个种群完美适应了某个特定环境、又能获得充足的资源，那就真的没有理由迁移或改变了。比如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年里几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的栖身之地。

cloze.title: 2023年6月·第2套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. After eating so much, you should be too full to eat another bite. But some people experience a powerful urge to keep eating, even after __(26)__ in a huge meal, a behavior that makes little sense, as most adults are well-versed in the dangers of obesity, which researchers have shown correlates with __(27)__ health issues and is even linked to increased __(28)__ risk. But some people still keep eating long after they should stop, a phenomenon Dr. Susan Thompson calls "insatiable(永不满足的) hunger." It is characterized by two main __(29)__ : not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary(久坐不动的).
passages.zh: 想象一下坐下来享用一顿丰盛的晚餐：一大块牛排、一大份炸土豆，还有蛋糕作为甜点。吃了这么多之后，你应该已经撑得一口也吃不下了。然而，有些人即使大吃了一顿，仍会产生继续进食的强烈冲动。这种行为似乎毫无道理，因为大多数成年人都十分了解肥胖的危害，而研究人员已经证明，肥胖与无数健康问题相关，甚至会增加死亡风险。但有些人即使早就应该停下，却仍然继续进食很久，这种现象被Susan Thompson博士称为“永不满足的饥饿”。它具有两个主要特征：进食后仍未感到满足，以及想要保持久坐不动的状态。

passages.en: This is at __(30)__ with how humans are biologically programmed. When there was a great deal of food available, ancient people would gorge on calories; this massive calorie intake was accompanied by an urge to get active. Humans were also programmed for something called "compensation," which is the brain's __(31)__ mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight. With compensation, if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally __(32)__ to eat less for the rest of the day.
passages.zh: 这与人类的生物本能相悖。当食物充足时，古人会大吃大喝，摄入大量热量；与此同时，他们还会产生进行活动的冲动。人类还被赋予了一种称为“补偿”的机制，即大脑防止体重过度增加的调节机制。借助这种补偿机制，如果你早上吃了一顿丰盛的饭，那么在当天剩余时间里，你自然会倾向于少吃一些。

passages.en: But recent studies show that 70% of American adults have lost the ability to naturally compensate for the calories they consume; worse __(33)__ , a significant number of them report __(34)__ hunger halfway through an eating session, but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down. Dr. Thompson argues that the main cause of this phenomenon is the modern diet, which is __(35)__ of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories.
passages.zh: 但近期研究表明，70%的美国成年人已经失去了对所摄入热量进行自然补偿的能力；更糟糕的是，其中相当一部分人表示，在进食过程中途，饥饿感会逐渐减弱，但到了用餐结束时，他们的饥饿程度却与刚坐下吃饭时相同，甚至更高。Thompson博士认为，这一现象的主要原因是现代饮食，而现代饮食由含有大量糖分、碳水化合物和热量的食物构成。

wordbank.gloss: 构成；be comprised of=由……组成（过去分词作形容词）
保护、保存（尤指自然资源）
正在减少的；逐渐递减（现在分词/动名词）

沉溺、放纵；indulge in=纵情享受、大吃大喝（动名词/现在分词）

仍然；更（用于比较级前加强语气）
无与伦比的、无法匹敌的

rows.text: H) indulging动词
介词 after 后必跟动名词

indulge in=纵情大吃，与“吃完一顿大餐”语义一致 句意是“即使在 indulging in a huge meal（沉溺/纵享一顿大餐）之后还想继续吃”，indulge in 是固定搭配，且语义恰是“尽情享用一顿大餐”，与开篇 Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. 的“暴饮暴食”场景严丝合缝。

B)comprised搭配是 be comprised of，不接 in comprised 的固定搭配是 be comprised of（由……组成），不与 in 连用，且这里没有 be 动词；语义“一顿大餐由……组成”也与“吃完后还想吃”的语境无关。 E)diminishing义为“递减”，与“暴饮暴食”反向 diminish in 表示“在……方面减少”，可这里要表达的是“纵享了一顿大餐”，diminishing in a huge meal（在一顿大餐中递减？）语义讲不通，方向恰好相反。
I) innumerable形容词
correlates with ___ health issues，名词前作定语
“无数的”健康问题，与肥胖危害的客观表述匹配 原文是说肥胖 correlates with __(27)__ health issues——医学常识告诉我们肥胖会引发“多到数不清”的健康问题（心血管、糖尿病、关节、肿瘤……），innumerable 是常见且中性的描述。
O)unmatchable感情色彩偏褒，且语义不通 unmatchable 表“无与伦比”，是积极/褒义评价词，用来形容“健康问题”从感情色彩到搭配都明显错位——说“无与伦比的健康问题”更像是把“好”和“坏”拼接起来，逻辑不通。
J) mortality名词
increased ___ risk，名词前作定语
mortality risk=死亡风险，肥胖危害的高频搭配 is even linked to increased __(28)__ risk. 上承“肥胖关联无数健康问题”，再用 even 递进，意指“甚至与死亡风险升高相关”——mortality risk 是医学英语里极常见的固定搭配，且 even 的递进语气也只有“死亡”这级别的代价能配得上。

A)attributesattribute risk 搭配不存在 attributes 是“属性”，与 risk 不能复合构成“属性风险”这种意义，且语义也不递进。 D)conservation话题错位 conservation 是“资源保护”，conservation risk 偏环保领域，与肥胖语境完全不接轨。 L)plights复数名词无法作单数前置定语，且无此搭配 plights 用复数，且 plights risk 不是固定搭配，无法表达“困境风险”这种意思。
A) attributes名词
two main ___ + 冒号后两项并列，需复数名词
attributes=特征，正好对应冒号后并列的两件特征 It is characterized by two main attributes：两个主要特征——一是“吃不饱”，二是“想久坐不动”，正好两条；attributes 在描写“现象/事物的标志性特征”时最常用，与 characterized by 形成 collocation 闭环。

D)conservation单数不可数，不能跟在 two main 后，且话题不对 conservation 一般不可数，前面带 two main 直接不合语法；语义“两个保护”也与“吃不饱+久坐”毫无关联。 L)plights感情色彩太重，且 characterized by plights 不自然 plights 强调“悲惨困境”，是悲剧色彩词；这里只是中性描述现象的两个特征，用“两大困境”过于戏剧化，且 be characterized by two main plights 不是地道搭配。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— plights 像“健康困境”，但搭配与色彩都不对。在 It is characterized by two main __(29)__ 处，plights（困境）看似贴“insatiable hunger 是种烦恼”，但 characterized by 后用 attributes/features 等中性词才地道；选 plights 既不搭配，也戏剧化。
K) odds名词
at__with 是介词框架，中间只能是名词
at odds with=与……相矛盾 段首正在做对比——“永不满足的饥饿”这件事 This is at __(30)__ with how humans are biologically programmed. 与人类生物程序“相矛盾”，at odds with 是这一意思的固定搭配，且段后描述古人“一吃多就想动”，正与“久坐不动”相反，逻辑闭环。

A)attributes无 at attributes with 搭配 attributes 作名词指“特征、属性”，没有 at attributes with 的固定结构，硬塞语义也不通。 D)conservation话题不对 conservation 指“资源保护”，与人体饮食机制毫无关联，且无 at conservation with 搭配。 J)mortality另有归宿，且无此搭配 mortality 是“死亡率”，要留给 28 空的 increased __ risk；且无 at mortality with 搭配。 L)plights无搭配，语义也不对 plight 是“困境”，没有 at plights with；说“这与生物程序处于困境”也不通顺。
M) regulatory形容词
the brain's ___ mechanism，名词前作定语
“调节性的”机制，与“防止体重过量积累”一一对应 compensation 被定义为 the brain's __(31)__ mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight.——“防止过量体重堆积”正是一种“调节、调控”的功能，regulatory mechanism（调节机制）是生理学常见搭配，语义贴合。

I)innumerable“无数的”修饰不可数的 mechanism 不通 innumerable 强调数量上无穷多，通常修饰复数可数名词；说“大脑无数的机制”既不贴合 a mechanism 的单数定指，也无法解释它“防止体重堆积”的具体功能。 O)unmatchable感情色彩偏褒，且不是科学常用搭配 unmatchable 意为“无与伦比”，是评价色彩词；下文是中性、客观的生理机制描述，且 unmatchable mechanism 几乎不出现于科学语篇。
G) inclined形容词
naturally ___ to do，be ___ to do 表语结构

be inclined to do=倾向做某事，唯一能接 to do be inclined to do 是固定搭配，意为“倾向于……”，正好对应“早上吃多了，剩下时间自然就少吃”的补偿逻辑：if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally __(32)__ to eat less for the rest of the day.
I)innumerable不接 to do innumerable 是“数不清的”，不与不定式连用，语法上直接不通；且语义“你是数不清的”更是荒谬。 O)unmatchable不接 to do，语义也不对 unmatchable 强调“无与伦比”，既无 be unmatchable to do 的常规结构，也与“倾向少吃”的中性补偿描述毫无关系。
N) still副词
worse ___ , 修饰比较级

worse still=更糟的是，固定插入语 六级里 worse still 是常用插入语，等同于 even worse / what's worse，专门承接更严重的事实——本句正是承接前文“补偿机制失灵”再升级，说“更糟的是相当多人吃到一半饥饿减弱、吃完反弹”，worse __(33)__, a significant number of them report __(34)__ hunger halfway through an eating session 语义一致。
F)farfar 修饰比较级须前置 far 强化比较级时位置是 far worse（远远更糟），不能写成 worse far；且 far 作插入语没有 worse far 这种习惯用法，结构不通。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— far 与 still 都能强化比较级，位置才是关键。看到 worse __(33)__ 极易选 far（far worse 在阅读里太常见），但本题空在 worse 之后，far 不能后置——记住 worse still 是固定插入语，far 必须前置。
E) diminishing动词
report ___ hunger，report 后接动名词或宾语

“饥饿感正在减弱”，与 halfway through 时点契合 句意是“相当多人报告吃到一半时 __ 饥饿感”——结合“饥饿感本应随进食而下降”的生理常识，diminishing hunger（正在减弱的饥饿感）正合理；后文 but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down. 用 but 转折，对照出“吃到一半饥饿在减弱，吃完反而又回来或更甚”，逻辑闭环。
B) comprised动词
be ___ of 被动/分词结构
be comprised of=由……组成 the modern diet, which is __(35)__ of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories. 句意为“现代饮食由高糖、高碳水、高热量的食物组成”，be comprised of 是该意的固定搭配，与全文“现代饮食是元凶”的结论严丝合缝。

longreading.title: 2023年6月·第2套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) When psychologist Jessica Pryor lived near an internationally renowned university, she once saw a student walking into a library holding a sleeping bag and a coffee maker. She has heard of graduate students spending 12 to 18 hours at a time in the lab. Their schedules are meant to be literally punishing: If they are scientists-in-training, they won't allow themselves to watch Netflix until their experiments start generating results. "Relationships become estranged(疏远的)—people stop inviting them to social gatherings or dinner parties, which leads them to spend even more time in the lab," Pryor told me.
passages.zh: 心理学家杰西卡·普赖尔住在一所国际知名大学附近时，曾看到一名学生拿着睡袋和咖啡机走进图书馆。她听说过研究生一次在实验室里待上12到18个小时。他们的日程安排简直是字面意义上的折磨：如果他们是接受科学家训练的学生，在实验开始产生结果之前，他们不会允许自己观看Netflix。“人际关系会变得疏远——人们不再邀请他们参加社交聚会或晚宴，这又导致他们把更多时间花在实验室里，”普赖尔告诉我。

passages.en: B) Along with other therapists, Pryor, who is now with the Family Institute at Northwestern University, is trying to sound the alarm about a tendency among young adults and college students to strive for perfection in their work—sometimes at any cost. Though it is often portrayed as a positive trait, Pryor and others say extreme perfectionism can lead to depression, anxiety, and even suicide.
passages.zh: 普赖尔如今供职于西北大学家庭研究所。她正与其他治疗师一道，试图就年轻人和大学生中一种不惜一切代价追求工作完美的倾向发出警告。尽管完美主义常常被描绘成一种积极的特质，但普赖尔等人表示，极端的完美主义可能导致抑郁、焦虑，甚至自杀。

passages.en: C) What's more, perfectionism seems to be on the rise. In a study of thousands of American, Canadian, and British college students published earlier this year, Thomas Curran of the University of Bath and Andrew Hill of York St. John University found that today's college students report higher levels of perfectionism than college students did during the 1990s or early 2000s. They measured three types of perfectionism: self-oriented, or a desire to be perfect; socially prescribed, or a desire to live up to others' expectations; and other-oriented, or holding others to unrealistic standards. From 1989 to 2016, they found, self-oriented perfectionism scores increased by 10 percent, socially prescribed scores rose by 33 percent, and other-oriented perfectionism increased by 16 percent.
passages.zh: 更重要的是，完美主义似乎正在日益盛行。在今年早些时候发表的一项针对数千名美国、加拿大和英国大学生的研究中，巴斯大学的托马斯·柯兰和约克圣约翰大学的安德鲁·希尔发现，如今的大学生报告的完美主义程度高于20世纪90年代或21世纪初的大学生。他们测量了三种完美主义：自我导向型，即渴望做到完美；社会规定型，即渴望达到他人的期望；以及他人导向型，即以不切实际的标准要求他人。他们发现，从1989年到2016年，自我导向型完美主义得分上升了10%，社会规定型得分上升了33%，他人导向型完美主义上升了16%。

passages.en: D) A person living with an other-oriented perfectionist might feel criticized by the perfectionist spouse for not doing household chores exactly the "right" way. "One of the most common things couples argue about is the proper way of loading the dishwasher," says Amy Bach, a psychologist in Providence, Rhode Island.
passages.zh: 与他人导向型完美主义者共同生活的人，可能会因为没有完全按照“正确”的方式做家务而受到完美主义伴侣的批评。“夫妻最常争论的事情之一，就是洗碗机应该如何正确装载，”罗德岛州普罗维登斯市的心理学家艾米·巴赫说。

passages.en: E) Curran describes socially prescribed perfectionism as "My self-esteem is contingent on what other people think." His study didn't examine the causal reasons for its rise, but he assumes that the rise of both standardized testing and social media might play a role. These days, LinkedIn alerts us when our rival gets a new job, and Instagram can let us know how well "liked" our lives are compared with a friend's. In an opinion piece earlier this year, Curran and Hill argue that society has also become more dog-eat-dog. "Over the last 50 years, public interest and civic responsibility have been progressively eroded," they write, "replaced by a focus on self-interest and competition in a supposedly free and open marketplace." We strive for perfection, it seems, because we feel we must in order to get ahead. Michael Brustein, a clinical psychologist in Manhattan, says when he first began practicing in 2007, he was surprised by how prevalent perfectionism was among his clients, despite how little his graduate training had focused on the phenomenon. He sees perfectionism in, among others, clients who are entrepreneurs, artists, and tech employees. "You're in New York because you're ambitious, you have this need to strive," he says. "But then your whole identity gets wrapped into a goal."
passages.zh: 柯兰将社会规定型完美主义描述为：“我的自尊取决于他人的看法。”他的研究没有考察这种完美主义上升的因果原因，但他认为，标准化考试和社交媒体的兴起可能都起了作用。如今，当竞争对手找到新工作时，LinkedIn会向我们发出提醒；而Instagram则能让我们知道，与朋友相比，我们的生活受到多少“点赞”。在今年早些时候的一篇评论文章中，柯兰和希尔认为，社会也变得更加弱肉强食。“在过去50年里，公众兴趣和公民责任逐渐受到侵蚀，”他们写道，“取而代之的是在一个所谓自由开放的市场中对自身利益和竞争的关注。”看来，我们之所以努力追求完美，是因为我们觉得自己必须这样做才能出人头地。曼哈顿的临床心理学家迈克尔·布鲁斯坦说，他于2007年开始执业时，尽管研究生阶段的训练很少关注这一现象，但他还是对完美主义在来访者中的普遍程度感到惊讶。在他的来访者中，有企业家、艺术家和科技公司员工等人表现出完美主义。“你身处纽约，是因为你有抱负，有这种不断进取的需要，”他说，“但随后，你的全部身份都被包裹在一个目标之中。”

passages.en: F) Perfectionism can, of course, be a positive force. Think of professional athletes, who train aggressively for ever-higher levels of competition. In well-adjusted perfectionism, someone who doesn't get the gold is able to forget the setback and move on. In maladaptive(不当的) perfectionism, meanwhile, people make an archive of all their failures. They revisit these archives constantly, thinking, as Pryor puts it, "I need to make myself feel terrible so I don't do this again." Then they double down, "raising the expectation bar even higher, which increases the likelihood of defeat, which makes you self-critical, so you raise the bar higher, work even harder," she says. Next comes failure, shame, and pushing yourself even harder toward even higher and more impossible goals. Meeting them becomes an "all or nothing" premise. Pryor offered this example: "Even if I'm an incredible attorney, if I don't make partner in the same pacing as one of my colleagues, clearly that means I'm a failure."
passages.zh: 当然，完美主义也可以是一种积极的力量。想想职业运动员吧，他们刻苦训练，以应对越来越高水平的竞争。在适应良好的完美主义中，一个没有获得金牌的人能够忘记这次挫折，继续前进。而在适应不良的完美主义中，人们会把自己所有的失败都整理成档案。他们不断回顾这些档案，像普赖尔所说的那样想着：“我需要让自己感觉很糟糕，这样我就不会再犯同样的错误。”然后他们会变本加厉，“把期望的标准提高得更高，这增加了失败的可能性，使你开始自我批评，于是你又把标准提高，工作更加努力，”她说。接下来便是失败、羞耻，以及把自己推向更高、更不可能实现的目标。达到这些目标成了一个“非此即彼”的前提。普赖尔举例说：“即使我是一个出色的律师，如果我没有和某位同事以同样的速度成为合伙人，那显然就意味着我是个失败者。”

passages.en: G) Brustein says his perfectionist clients tend to devalue their accomplishments, so that every time a goal is achieved, the high lasts only a short time, like "a gas tank with a hole in it." If the boss says you did a great job, it's because he doesn't know anything. If the audience likes your work, that's because it's too stupid to know what good art actually is. But, therapists say, there are also different ways perfectionism manifests. Some perfectionists are always pushing themselves forward. But others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect. Or they might handicap their performance ahead of time. They're the ones partying until 2 a.m. the night before the final, so that when the grade C rolls in, there's a ready excuse.
passages.zh: 布鲁斯坦说，他的完美主义来访者往往会贬低自己的成就，因此每当实现一个目标时，兴奋感只会持续很短时间，就像“一个有洞的油箱”。如果老板说你工作做得很好，那是因为他什么都不懂。如果观众喜欢你的作品，那是因为他们太愚蠢，不知道真正优秀的艺术是什么。但治疗师们说，完美主义也有不同的表现方式。有些完美主义者总是在推动自己向前。然而，另一些人实际上会在工作上落后，因为除非作业达到完美，否则他们就无法完成。或者，他们可能会提前削弱自己的表现。他们就是那些在期末考试前一晚一直狂欢到凌晨两点的人，这样当C等成绩公布时，他们就有了现成的借口。

passages.en: H) While educators and parents have successfully convinced students of the need to be high performing and diligent, the experts told me, they haven't adequately prepared them for the inevitability of failure. Instead of praises like "You're so smart," parents and educators should say things like "You really stuck with it," Pryor says, to emphasize the value of perseverance over intrinsic talent. Pryor notes that many of her clients are wary she'll "turn them into some degenerate couch potato and teach them to be okay with it." Instead, she tries to help them think through the parts of their perfectionism they'd like to keep, and to lose the parts that are ruining their lives.
passages.zh: 专家告诉我，尽管教育工作者和父母已经成功地让学生认识到取得优异成绩和勤奋努力的必要性，但他们没有充分让学生为失败不可避免这一事实做好准备。普赖尔说，父母和教育工作者不应说“你真聪明”之类的夸奖，而应说“你真的坚持下来了”之类的话，以强调毅力相对于天赋的重要性。普赖尔指出，她的许多来访者担心她会“把他们变成某种无所事事、整天躺在沙发上的人，并教他们接受这种状态”。相反，她会努力帮助他们想清楚自己的完美主义中哪些部分是他们想保留的，哪些部分正在毁掉他们的生活，应当舍弃。

passages.en: I) Bach, who sees many students from Brown University, says some of them don't even go out on weekends, let alone weekdays. She tells them, "Aim high, but get comfortable with good enough." When they don't get some award, she encourages them to remember that "one outcome is not a basis for a broad conclusion about the person's intelligence, qualifications, or potential for the future."
passages.zh: 经常接诊布朗大学学生的巴赫说，其中一些人周末都不出门，更不用说工作日了。她告诉他们：“目标要定得高，但要适应做到足够好。”当他们没有获得某个奖项时，她会鼓励他们记住：“一次结果不能作为对一个人的智力、资历或未来潜力作出广泛结论的依据。”

passages.en: J) The treatment for perfectionism might be as simple as having patients keep logs of things they can be proud of, or having them behave imperfectly in small ways, just to see how it feels. "We might have them hang the towels crooked(不正的) or wear some clothing inside out," says Martin Antony, a professor in the department of psychology at Ryerson University in Toronto.
passages.zh: 对完美主义的治疗可能简单到让患者记录下自己值得自豪的事情，或者让他们以一些小的方式表现得不完美，只是为了看看那是什么感觉。“我们可能会让他们把毛巾挂得歪一些，或者把衣服反穿，”多伦多瑞尔森大学心理学系教授马丁·安东尼说。

passages.en: K) Brustein likes to get his perfectionist clients to create values that are important to them, then try to shift their focus to living according to those values rather than achieving specific goals. It's a play on the "You really stuck with it" message for kids. In other words, it isn't about doing a headstand in yoga class; it's about going to yoga class in the first place, because you like to be the kind of person who takes care of herself. But he warns that some people go into therapy expecting too much—an instant transformation of themselves from a pathological(病态的) perfectionist to a (still high-achieving) non-perfectionist. They try to be perfect, in other words, at no longer being perfect.
passages.zh: 布鲁斯坦喜欢让他的完美主义来访者确立对他们来说重要的价值观，然后试着把注意力转向按照这些价值观生活，而不是实现具体目标。这是对“你真的坚持下来了”这句话在孩子身上的运用。换句话说，重点不是在瑜伽课上完成头倒立，而是首先去上瑜伽课，因为你喜欢成为一个会照顾自己的人。但他警告说，有些人接受心理治疗时期望过高，想要自己从一个病态的完美主义者立即转变成一个（仍然成就很高的）非完美主义者。换句话说，他们试图在不再完美这件事上做到完美。

passages.en: How on earth did we come to this? We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.
passages.zh: 我们究竟是如何走到这一步的？我们近乎偏执地保护孩子免受一切伤害；我们审查与他们接触的每一位看护人、教师或医生。然而，尽管做到了这一切，一个绝非一心为了孩子最大利益着想的群体，却几乎可以无拘无束地接触到他们。

passages.en: We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.
passages.zh: 我们似乎理所当然地认为，广告商和营销人员被允许去塑造哪怕是最年幼的孩子。在孩子们甚至还没建立起对自我身份的正确认知，或学会管理金钱之前，他们就被鼓励将社会地位和自我价值与物质挂钩，并寻求名声和财富等外在事物来证明自己。我们正在培养微型消费者，而不是那些会因自己对所生活的社会做出贡献而珍视自身价值的青年公民。

passages.en: We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it. It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents. We've come to know it as "pester power" or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases.
passages.zh: 我们走到这一步是如此循序渐进，以至于我们当中的许多人从未对此提出过质疑。在广告商开始针对年轻人、并发现可以招募他们对其父母发起商业冲击以来的60年里，这一切已经悄然潜入我们的生活。我们逐渐将其称为“缠人力量”（pester power），即儿童施压父母做出某些购买行为的能力。

passages.en: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.
passages.zh: 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育工作者指出，研究表明这种兴起的“从摇篮到坟墓”的消费主义正在导致自卑、抑郁和其他形式心理疾病的发生率不断上升。

passages.en: Not all psychologists agree. There're plenty working hand in glove with a ￡12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form—often literally. It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children. Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood.
passages.zh: 并非所有心理学家都持赞同意见。有许多心理学家与这个年产值达120亿英镑的产业密切合作，该产业已将对成年人情感和欲望的操纵变成了一门艺术形式——往往字面意义上确实如此。该产业还在不断开发新方法来劝诱我们的孩子渴望物质财产，并且由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需要感染少数人就能传播给大众。广告和营销对儿童也能起到有益的作用。营销可能有助于促进儿童作为消费者的社会化，向他们提供产品信息，并帮助他们在迈入成年期时树立独特的自我身份。

passages.en: Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children? I say yes.
passages.zh: 那么，我们是否应该禁止所有针对幼童的广告？我的答案是肯定的。

passages.en: Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s. There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.
passages.zh: 当然，全面禁止面向11岁以下儿童的广告必然会引发大量反对意见。有些人会辩称，这将是对言论自由的侵犯，并侵犯了企业通过给幼童洗脑来让他们索要其产品的权利。

passages.en: Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions. And though advertising is only part of an all-pervasive(无处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere. Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now.
passages.zh: 大多数父母都憎恨广告对其孩子产生的影响，但我们确实有能力终结它，让我们的孩子在成长过程中免受消费主义诸多压力的困扰，直到他们大到足以做出自己的决定。尽管广告只是无处不在的营销文化的一部分，但我们需要从某个地方开始。让我们现在就禁止所有针对小学及以下年龄儿童的广告。

questions.stem: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children?
questions.stem_zh: 作者说哪一群体几乎可以不受限制地接触儿童?

options.text: Advertisers.
options.zh: 广告商。

options.text: Carers.
options.zh: 看护者。

options.text: Teachers.
options.zh: 教师。

options.text: Doctors.
options.zh: 医生。

questions.判型: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children? 直接询问「哪一群人」，要求在原文里找出对应群体，是典型的事实细节追问。
questions.拆句: 主干为 Which group of people ... has almost unrestricted access to children，does the author say 是插入语，去掉后剩「哪一群人对孩子有几乎不受限制的接触权」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access. 然而尽管如此，有一个群体，他们丝毫不把孩子的最大利益放在心上，却几乎不受限制地接触着孩子。

locate.en: Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.
locate.zh: 然而尽管如此，有一个群体，他们丝毫不把孩子的最大利益放在心上，却几乎不受限制地接触着孩子。

option_analysis.note: 预判的「对孩子不友好却不受限制的群体」在 P2 被明示为广告商和营销者，与选项 Advertisers 直接对应。

pairs.orig: advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children

option_analysis.note: Carers 属于 every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact 中被严格审查的一方，是「保护孩子」的角色，与「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体相反。
Teachers 同样位于 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中，是被审查的对象，不是「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体。
Doctors 也是 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中的被审查对象，原文未把医生列为「几乎不受限接触孩子」的群体。

questions.stem: What kind of people should we enable children to become according to the author?
questions.stem_zh: 根据作者的观点,我们应该让儿童成为什么样的人?

options.text: Those who look to fame and wealth for external and ultimate validation.
options.zh: 那些寻求名利以获得外在和终极认可的人。

options.text: Those who value themselves because of their contribution to society.
options.zh: 那些因为对社会的贡献而重视自己的人。

options.text: Those who associate self-worth with the ability to handle money.
options.zh: 那些将自我价值与处理金钱的能力联系起来的人。

options.text: Those who have developed a proper sense of their own identity.
options.zh: 那些已经形成了对自身身份认同的恰当意识的人。

questions.判型: What kind of people should we enable children to become according to the author? 含 according to the author，要求复述原文已写明的内容，不要求跨段综合，仍是细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干为 What kind of people should we enable children to become，become 后省略表语补足语，由四个选项的 Those who... 补齐；结构清楚，唯一要注意的是 enable children to become＝「让孩子成长为」，主语是 we 不是 children。
questions.定位: P2 We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live. 我们正在培养小消费者，而不是会因自己对所在社会的贡献而看重自身价值的年轻公民。

locate.en: We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.
locate.zh: 我们正在培养小消费者，而不是会因自己对所在社会的贡献而看重自身价值的年轻公民。

option_analysis.note: Those who look to fame and wealth for external and ultimate validation 对应 to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation，是作者批判而非倡导的形象。
选项 B 在主语「Those who」、动词「value themselves」、原因状语三处与定位句逐项对应，是作者正向倡导项的同义改写。

pairs.orig: young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live
pairs.opt: Those who value themselves because of their contribution to society

option_analysis.note: Those who associate self-worth with the ability to handle money 把 learned to handle money 这个被作者列出的「尚未具备」的前提，偷换成孩子应该成为的目标。
Those who have developed a proper sense of their own identity 同样取自 Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity，仅是作者列出的孩子尚未具备的前提，并非最终倡导项。

questions.stem: Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____.
questions.stem_zh: 许多儿童发展专家和教育工作者呼吁关注研究,这些研究表明_____。

options.text: life-long consumerism is causing more and more cases of psychological problems.
options.zh: 终身消费主义正在导致越来越多的心理问题病例。

options.text: increasing commercialization of education is eroding many children's self-esteem.
options.zh: 教育日益商业化正在侵蚀许多儿童的自尊。

options.text: the growing desire for wealth is contributing to a rising rate of depression.
options.zh: 对财富日益增长的渴望正在导致抑郁症发病率上升。

options.text: the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life.
options.zh: 对购买物质产品的渴望在人的一生中被培养起来。

questions.判型: Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____. 是不完整陈述句，要求选项填入研究的内容，等同于追问该研究的结论事实，归为细节题。
questions.拆句: 主句 Many child development experts and educators call attention to research，that suggests 后续宾语从句由选项补齐；call attention to＝呼吁关注，是熟词僻义提醒，主语动作就是「指出研究表明……」。
questions.定位: P4 Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness. 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育者援引研究指出：这种正在出现的「从摇篮到坟墓」的消费主义，正在导致低自尊、抑郁和其他形式心理疾病的发生率不断上升。

locate.en: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.
locate.zh: 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育者援引研究指出：这种正在出现的「从摇篮到坟墓」的消费主义，正在导致低自尊、抑郁和其他形式心理疾病的发生率不断上升。

option_analysis.note: 选项 A 的主语「终生消费主义」、谓语「正在导致」、宾语「越来越多心理问题」与定位句三项要点逐一同义对应，是最精确的复述。

pairs.orig: growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness
pairs.opt: more and more cases of psychological problems

option_analysis.note: increasing commercialization of education 在原文中完全没有提及，作者批评的是面向孩子的广告与营销，不是教育自身的商业化。
the growing desire for wealth 只是原文 fame and wealth 的一半；a rising rate of depression 也只是 low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness 的一项。两处都只取了原文的局部。
the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life 说的是「物欲是如何被培养起来的」，而题干要求复述「研究表明的因果结论」——D 项把因果关系换成了「物欲是如何形成」，与题干追问方向不一致。

questions.stem: What does the author imply about the impact of advertising?
questions.stem_zh: 关于广告的影响,作者暗示了什么?

options.text: It is actually infectious to many rather than a few.
options.zh: 它实际上会传染给许多人而不是少数人。

options.text: It is rooted in our desire for material possessions.
options.zh: 它植根于我们对物质财产的欲望。

options.text: It is comparable to that of virus.
options.zh: 它可与病毒的影响相比。

options.text: It is literally limited to children.
options.zh: 它实际上仅限于儿童。

questions.判型: What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 中的 imply 表明本题要求基于原文作推断，而非复述事实。
questions.拆句: What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 主干是 What ... the author imply，about the impact of advertising 限定推断对象；句子简洁，需注意 imply 是「暗示」而非「明示」。
questions.定位: P5 It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. 它（广告业）也是这样一个行业：不断开发新方法来诱使我们的孩子渴望物质；而由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需感染少数即可触及多数。

locate.en: It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many.
locate.zh: 它（广告业）也是这样一个行业：不断开发新方法来诱使我们的孩子渴望物质；而由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需感染少数即可触及多数。

option_analysis.note: 由 infect a few to reach the many 一步推出「广告其实波及多数而非少数」，正好是 imply 题所要的「一步推断」型答案。

pairs.orig: they only need to infect a few to reach the many
pairs.opt: It is actually infectious to many rather than a few

pairs.orig: they only need to infect a few to reach the many

option_analysis.note: rooted in our desire for material possessions 把因果反过来——原文是「广告诱使孩子产生物欲」（persuade our children to desire material possessions），不是「广告源于物欲」。
comparable to that of virus 已经超出原文 viral effect 的比喻：原文只说「影响具有病毒式扩散效应」，并没断言「广告影响可与病毒影响相提并论」。两者程度差异明显。
literally limited to children 把广告影响范围缩限到「仅限于儿童」，而原文 infect a few to reach the many 恰恰强调影响会扩散到「多数」，并非「仅限于儿童」。

questions.stem: What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children?
questions.stem_zh: 反对者针对完全禁止向幼儿做广告提出了什么论点?

options.text: It would deprive them of the chance to learn about products.
options.zh: 这会剥夺他们了解产品的机会。

options.text: It would render them unable to carve out unique identities.
options.zh: 这会使他们无法塑造独特的身份认同。

options.text: It would breach their freedom as would-be consumers.
options.zh: 这会侵犯他们作为潜在消费者的自由。

options.text: It would violate the rights endowed upon advertisers.
options.zh: 这会侵犯赋予广告商的权利。

questions.判型: What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children? 直接问反对者给出的具体论据，对应原文中已写明的让步句，属细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is the opponents' argument，against a complete ban on advertising to young children 是后置修饰，整体含义是「反对者反对彻底禁广告时给出的理由」；注意 against 修饰的是 argument，而非整个句子的否定。
questions.定位: P7 There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products. 会有人辩称（禁止广告）将构成对言论自由的侵犯，并损害企业「向幼儿洗脑、让他们索要产品」的权利。

locate.en: There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.
locate.zh: 会有人辩称（禁止广告）将构成对言论自由的侵犯，并损害企业「向幼儿洗脑、让他们索要产品」的权利。

option_analysis.note: deprive them of the chance to learn about products 取自 Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products，是作者描述广告「益处」的内容，并非 P7 中的反方论据。
render them unable to carve out unique identities 同样取自 help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood，是广告作为「益处」的功能描述，非 P7 中反方对禁令的反对理由。
breach their freedom as would-be consumers 中 their 指 young children；但 a breach of freedom of speech 中被侵犯的是「言论自由」，主语暗指「企业表达自由」，不是「孩子作为准消费者的自由」。
反方第二条论据「损害企业的权利」被选项 D 完整同义改写为「侵犯广告商被赋予的权利」，且两条论据中只有该条被选项明确复述。

pairs.orig: infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products
pairs.opt: violate the rights endowed upon advertisers

pairs.orig: the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products

reading2.title: 2023年6月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used "non-traditional" monitoring techniques on staff last year.
passages.zh: 许多人反对职场监控，因为它本身具有非人化的影响，而且会带来持续不断的压力。但随着各公司寻求通过从员工身上榨取更多生产力来提高效率，职场监控正在世界各地日益普及。去年，年收入超过7.5亿美元的公司中，有一半以上采用了对员工进行“非传统”监控的技术。

passages.en: Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather "data exhaust" left by employees' email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.
passages.zh: 监控员工的工作表现使公司能够评估员工的工作状况及其互动方式，这对公司和员工自身都可能有益。越来越多的分析公司提供这项服务。它们收集员工电子邮件和即时通信应用留下的“数据尾迹”，并使用配备射频识别装置和麦克风的胸牌。这些设备可以检查你花了多少时间交谈、你的说话音量和语调，甚至还能判断你是否主导了谈话。虽然这听起来可能具有侵扰性，但支持者认为，它也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。

passages.en: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
passages.zh: 其中一些数据分析可能会产生意想不到的结果。例如，人们发现，坐在可容纳12人的餐桌旁的人往往比经常坐在四人桌旁的人进行更多互动、分享更多想法，工作表现也更出色；如果没有这种数据分析，这一事实很可能不会被发现。

passages.en: Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular "chipping parties", where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.
passages.zh: 在过去几年里，斯德哥尔摩一个名为Epicenter的共享办公空间走得更远，举办颇受欢迎的“植入芯片派对”，人们可以将微型芯片植入手中。他们可以利用这些植入物开启电子控制的门，或者监测打字速度与心率之间的相关性。植入式芯片似乎很极端，但从身份证件和生物识别技术发展到这类设备，其实只是一小步。

passages.en: As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
passages.zh: 只要这类方案是自愿的，面向便利性的用途可能会越来越多，从而使相当多的员工愿意植入芯片。但如果植入式芯片被用来减少空闲时间或休息时间，就可能造成不利影响。而且，如果监控工具剥夺了人们的自主权，它们就会变得最不受欢迎。许多方面取决于如何传达这些监控举措，而恰当的沟通可能会防止潜在的反抗发生。

passages.en: If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
passages.zh: 如果老板不能进行有效沟通，员工就会做最坏的猜测。但如果老板公开说明他们正在收集哪些信息以及如何使用这些信息，研究表明，46%的员工通常能够接受。尽管许多此类监控方案使用匿名化数据，且参与是自愿的，许多员工仍然持怀疑态度，并担心自己的公民自由受到侵蚀。

passages.en: So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.
passages.zh: 因此，职场监控可能会赋予员工更多权能，也可能对寻求提高效率和盈利能力的公司有所帮助。但如果实施方式不当，它也可能变成一种不受欢迎的压迫工具，最终适得其反。

questions.stem: Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么许多人反对监控员工绩效?

options.text: It puts workers under constant pressure.
options.zh: 它使员工处于持续的压力之下。

options.text: It is universally deemed anti-human by nature.
options.zh: 它被普遍认为本质上是反人性的。

options.text: It does both mental and physical harm to employees monitored.
options.zh: 它对被监控的员工造成精神和身体上的伤害。

options.text: It enables firms to squeeze maximal productivity from employees.
options.zh: 它使企业能够从员工身上榨取最大的生产力。

questions.判型: 题干Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?直接索取一个被作者写在文中的客观原因,而非作者本人的推断或态度。
questions.拆句: 题干主干为被动语态are...opposed to,opposed to后接动名词短语monitoring employee performance作介词宾语;句首Why仅起询问原因作用,无陷阱结构。
questions.定位: P1 Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. 许多人反对工作场所监控,因为它本身具有非人化的效果,并且带来持续不断的压力。

locate.en: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings.
locate.zh: 许多人反对工作场所监控,因为它本身具有非人化的效果,并且带来持续不断的压力。

option_analysis.note: 预判中"持续压力"一条被A项constant pressure逐词同义对应,A为定位句两项理由之一的精确改写,在四个选项中是唯一与原文有同义映射的项。
原文说监控具有inherent dehumanizing effect,只是描述其内在属性,并未声称这一点被普遍认同;B项把它升级为universally deemed anti-human,把"内在属性"偷换为"举世公认"。
原文只提及dehumanizing effect与relentless pressure,均偏心理与人格层面;C项添加physical harm,原文无任何关于身体伤害的表述。
squeeze maximal productivity复述的是企业立场——原文firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers是企业实施监控的动机,而非员工反对的理由,角色彻底错位。

questions.stem: What is the supporters' argument for workplace surveillance?
questions.stem_zh: 支持者对工作场所监控的论据是什么?

options.text: It enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations.
options.zh: 它使员工能够避免主导谈话。

options.text: It enhances employees' identification with firms they work in.
options.zh: 它增强员工对其所在企业的认同感。

options.text: It can alert employees to intrusion into their privacy.
options.zh: 它可以提醒员工注意对其隐私的侵犯。

options.text: It can protect employees against aggressive behavior.
options.zh: 它可以保护员工免受攻击性行为的伤害。

questions.判型: 题干What is the supporters' argument直接索取支持方在文中明说的一项主张,不要求读者推断弦外之音。
questions.拆句: 题干为What引导的特殊疑问句,系动词is后接名词短语the supporters' argument for workplace surveillance,for短语作定语限定argument的对象,结构平直无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment. 尽管这听起来具有侵扰性,支持者主张监控也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。

locate.en: While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.
locate.zh: 尽管这听起来具有侵扰性,支持者主张监控也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。

option_analysis.note: 原文These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations.是描述"监控能检测谈话占比"的功能,而非支持方提出的argument;A项enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations把"检测是否dominate"扭曲为"使员工避免dominate"。
B项enhances employees' identification with firms谈的是员工对公司的认同感,原文整段无任何提及"员工认同公司"的语义。
原文While this may sound intrusive承认监控"听起来侵犯隐私",但支持者的argument是against bullying而非against intrusion;C项alert employees to intrusion into their privacy反而把"监控可警示员工隐私被侵犯"作为主张,与支持方立场相反。
预判中的"保护员工免受bullying与sexual harassment"被D项以aggressive behavior一词概括,protect...against结构原样保留,是定位句的标准同义替换。

pairs.orig: protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment

questions.stem: What does the author want to show by the example of different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables?
questions.stem_zh: 作者想通过午餐桌上不同人数互动的例子说明什么?

options.text: Data analysis is key to the successful implementation of workplace surveillance.
options.zh: 数据分析是成功实施工作场所监控的关键。

options.text: Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
options.zh: 分析从员工那里收集的数据可以产生意想不到的结果。

options.text: More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
options.zh: 更多同事坐在一张午餐桌旁往往有助于互动和想法分享。

options.text: It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.
options.zh: 没有数据分析,很难决定一张午餐桌应该坐多少人。

questions.判型: What does the author want to show by the example...中by the example明示题干在追问例子的论证目的而非例子的字面内容。
questions.拆句: 题干主干What...want to show中by the example为方式状语,后接of介词短语different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables修饰example;considering动名词成分较长,但句意线性无歧义。
questions.定位: P3 Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis. 这种数据分析有时会产生出人意料的结果。例如,研究发现坐12人餐桌的人比坐4人餐桌的人更倾向于互动、分享想法,表现也更好,而这一事实如果没有这种数据分析很可能会被忽略。

locate.en: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
locate.zh: 这种数据分析有时会产生出人意料的结果。例如,研究发现坐12人餐桌的人比坐4人餐桌的人更倾向于互动、分享想法,表现也更好,而这一事实如果没有这种数据分析很可能会被忽略。

B项主谓宾三段(Analyzing data/can yield/something unexpected)与原文(this data analysis/can produce/unexpected results)逐成分对应,是论点句的标准同义重写。

pairs.opt: Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.

option_analysis.note: C项More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing字面复述了例子内容,但题干问的是例子要说明的论点,不是例子本身,答非所问。
原文末尾a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis强调的是"数据分析揭示了这一事实",而非"数据分析帮助决定餐桌人数";D项把焦点偏到"决定餐桌坐几人"上。

questions.stem: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?
questions.stem_zh: 监控措施的大部分积极效果取决于什么?

options.text: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
options.zh: 员工被监控的频率。

options.text: What specific personal information is being excluded.
options.zh: 哪些具体的个人信息被排除在外。

options.text: What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
options.zh: 采取了哪些措施来最大限度地减少其有害影响。

options.text: How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.
options.zh: 老板们如何充分说明其监控目的。

questions.判型: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?问的是文中明确写出的依赖条件,不需推断。
questions.拆句: 题干主干What does...depend on?中谓语动词是depend on,主语是较长的名词短语much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives;of短语层层修饰,但语义线性,认出动词短语depend on即可。
questions.定位: P5 A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged. 很多事情取决于这些监控举措是如何被传达的,这种沟通可能阻止潜在的抵制行动发生。

locate.en: A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
locate.zh: 很多事情取决于这些监控举措是如何被传达的,这种沟通可能阻止潜在的抵制行动发生。

option_analysis.note: 原文从未提到监控的frequency(频率),只谈how communicated;A项把"如何沟通"偷换为"多频繁地监控",原文无任何对应。
原文many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data谈匿名化处理,但语境是"虽然匿名,员工仍恐惧";B项specific personal information is being excluded把焦点偏到"排除哪些信息",且与题干"positive effect depend on"无对应。
原文确实提到detrimental一词,但句子是"如果用监控减少休息,可能detrimental";题干问的是"positive effect depend on",答案应回到A lot depends on的主句而非detrimental前的条件句;C项把"减少不利影响的步骤"作为positive effect的依赖,属过度推断。
D项核心动词make known精确对应原文communicated,主语bosses合理补出施动者,purpose of monitoring为补全语境的合理增添,语义聚焦于"沟通"这一关键变量。

pairs.opt: How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring

questions.拆句: 题干主干What concern do monitoring initiatives cause中concern作cause的宾语前置,among many staffers为范围状语;倒装并未改变句意,主语是monitoring initiatives。

locate.en: Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
locate.zh: 尽管许多此类监控方案使用匿名数据且参与是自愿的,许多员工仍持怀疑态度,担心他们的公民自由被侵蚀。

option_analysis.note: 原文workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff中的empower指的是"赋权员工",而非"赋权雇主";A项empower employers excessively反转了方向,且excessively无原文支撑。

translation.title: 2023年6月·第2套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 城市公共设施改善的社会现象介绍 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 随着中国经济的快速发展和人们生活水平的稳步提高,城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高。中国地方政府更加注重公共设施的建设和改进,以更好地满足人们的需求。通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造,许多城市为市民提供了更多休闲和社交的场所。 如今,政府出资购置的健身器械和铺设的健身步道在不少城市随处可见,既明显改善了市民户外活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽。
translation.reference_en:
With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards, urban residents are placing increasingly high demands on the environment and the quality of life. To meet these rising demands, Chinese local governments are attaching greater importance to the construction and improvement of public facilities. By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas, many cities have provided their citizens with more places for leisure and social activities. Today, government-funded fitness equipment and newly paved fitness trails can be seen everywhere in many cities, which has not only markedly improved the conditions for residents' outdoor activities but also made the cities more beautiful.
【衔接】
句1→句2:补'因此/响应需求'的因果承接句1说居民要求越来越高 城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高,句2说政府更加注重建设 中国地方政府更加注重公共设施的建设和改进,二者是'需求上升→政府回应'的因果。句2句首可补 In response 或 To meet these rising demands 承上,让逻辑显形,而非两句干放。
句2→句3:用具体举措承接抽象做法句2讲政府'注重建设和改进'(抽象),句3 通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地 是这一做法的具体落地。可在句3前用 For example 或直接以 By building… 的方式状语自然衔接,体现'总—分'关系。
句4:用 Today 标出时间、与全篇现状呼应句4以 如今→Today 开头,标明这是当下可见的结果,呼应全篇'现状'基调,作为收束句把前文举措落到'市民已能享受到的实效'。

cohesion.detail: 句4以 如今→Today 开头,标明这是当下可见的结果,呼应全篇'现状'基调,作为收束句把前文举措落到'市民已能享受到的实效'。

main_idea.core: 城市公共设施改善的社会现象介绍
main_idea.detail: 这段属于社会现象/民生类客观介绍。开篇 随着中国经济的快速发展和人们生活水平的稳步提高,城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高 摆出背景与现状,随后讲政府如何回应需求、改善公共设施,通篇是对当下普遍事实的客观陈述,语体平实、不带主观抒情。这决定了全篇以现在时为主、用词偏正式书面。

tense.detail: 通篇在陈述当下普遍存在的事实与趋势——居民要求越来越高、政府更加注重建设、设施随处可见,都是现在的状态而非已结束的往事,故全篇以一般现在时为基调。如 城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高、在不少城市随处可见 都是现在的现状。仅个别表'已完成动作'处(如'改善了')可酌用现在完成时,但默认回此基调。

term_notes.detail: 统一译为 public facilities。公共设施的建设和改进 中的核心词,facilities 此处指公共配套设备/场所,惯用复数;全篇凡指此概念只用这一译法,不要一会儿 public utilities 一会儿 public infrastructure 来回换。
统一译为 public green spaces(或 green areas)。公园和公共绿地 中的文化/民生负载词,指城市里的成片绿化用地,用 green spaces 比直译 green land 地道;green 为可数搭配,用复数 spaces。
统一译为 fitness trails。铺设的健身步道 是较新的本土设施名,trail 指供步行/锻炼的小径,配 fitness 表健身用途;与前文 fitness equipment(健身器械)成对,全篇一致用 fitness 这一限定词。

steps.text: 主语=城市居民,谓语=要求越来越高（主语策略：原句主语）中文已给出明确主语 城市居民对环境和生活品质的要求越来越高,直接用它作英文主语:urban residents。主干立为 urban residents have increasingly high expectations / demand more and more,宾语是 for the environment and quality of life。句首 随着中国经济的快速发展和人们生活水平的稳步提高 是背景,不进主干。

随着…→With 引导的伴随状语随着中国经济的快速发展和人们生活水平的稳步提高 不是主干,降级成 With 引导的介词短语作状语:With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards,置于句首,后接主句。两个并列的'发展/提高'用 and 连接两个名词短语,而非各起一个分句,避免拖成流水句。

时态回指全篇基调用一般现在时:demand / have expectations,陈述当下普遍现状。 单复数城市居民不止一人→urban residents 用复数;相应谓语用复数 have / demand。 程度词'越来越高'是递增,用 increasingly high 或 more and more,别只译成 high 丢掉'越来越'的递增义。 搭配'对…的要求'用 demand for sth 或 expectations for / of sth,介词搭配固定,别用 require to。

With the rapid development of China's economy and the steady improvement of people's living standards, urban residents are placing increasingly high demands on the environment and the quality of life.
主语=地方政府,谓语=注重建设和改进（主语策略：原句主语）中国地方政府更加注重公共设施的建设和改进 主语明确是'地方政府',直接作英文主语 local governments;谓语 pay more attention to / attach greater importance to;宾语是'公共设施的建设和改进'。句末 以更好地满足人们的需求 是目的,不进主干。
以…→to do 目的状语以更好地满足人们的需求 表目的,降级成不定式 to better meet people's needs 作目的状语,接在主句后。'建设和改进'两个并列名词作 to 的宾语:the construction and improvement of public facilities,不必拆成两个分句。

时态回指基调用一般现在时:local governments pay / attach,陈述当前做法。 单复数'地方政府'指各地多个政府→local governments 用复数,谓语随之用复数 pay / attach。 搭配'注重'用 attach (greater) importance to / pay more attention to,后接名词;'满足需求'用 meet/satisfy one's needs,needs 用复数。
Chinese local governments are attaching greater importance to the construction and improvement of public facilities in order to better meet people's needs.
主语=许多城市,谓语=提供了场所（主语策略：原句主语）许多城市为市民提供了更多休闲和社交的场所 主语是'许多城市'→many cities,谓语 provide / offer,宾语 more places for leisure and social activities。句首一大串 通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造 是方式,不进主干。

通过…→By doing 方式状语通过兴建新的广场、公园和公共绿地或对原有公共场地重新加以规划改造 译成 By 引导的动名词方式状语:By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas。其中'兴建……'与'重新规划改造……'是两种并列方式,用 or 连接两个 doing 结构;'广场、公园和公共绿地'是三个并列宾语,A, B and C 列举。

时态'提供了'带完成义,可用现在完成时 have provided 强调已带来的结果;若与全篇统一也可用一般现在时 provide。本句宜用 have provided,既不悖基调又点出'已经提供'的完成感。 单复数广场/公园/绿地都不止一处→squares, parks, public green spaces 全用复数;'许多城市'→many cities;'场所'→places 复数。 结构平行or 连接的两个方式须同形:building… 对 redesigning and renovating…,都用 -ing 动名词,别一个 -ing 一个 to do。 搭配'为…提供…'用 provide sb with sth 或 provide sth for sb;'休闲和社交的场所'→places for leisure and social activities。

By building new squares, parks and public green spaces, or redesigning and renovating existing public areas, many cities have provided their citizens with more places for leisure and social activities.

主语=健身器械和健身步道,谓语=随处可见（主语策略：原句主语）政府出资购置的健身器械和铺设的健身步道在不少城市随处可见 的主语是'健身器械和健身步道'→fitness equipment and fitness trails,谓语'随处可见'→can be seen everywhere / are commonly seen。'政府出资购置的''铺设的'是修饰主语的定语,不进主干;句末 既明显改善了市民户外活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽 是补充结果。

定语→过去分词;既…又…→并列谓语'政府出资购置的''铺设的'两个定语用过去分词降级:fitness equipment funded by the government and fitness trails it has paved(或合并为 government-funded fitness equipment and paved trails)。句末 既明显改善了市民户外活动的条件,又使城市更加美丽 是'随处可见'带来的双重效果,用 which 引导的非限定定语从句 + 并列谓语收尾:which not only … but also …,避免另起流水句。

时态'随处可见'是现状→现在时 can be seen / are commonly seen;'改善了'带完成义可用现在完成时 have improved,与基调不冲突。 语态'随处可见''出资购置的''铺设的'都隐含被动(被看见/被购置/被铺设),英文用被动 can be seen / funded by / paved,符合英文被动多于汉语的习惯。 单复数fitness equipment 是不可数名词,作主语时谓语单复数取决于并列:equipment and trails 两者并列→谓语用复数 are / can be seen;trails 用复数。 关联词'既…又…'用 not only … but also …;若 not only 提到句首需部分倒装,放从句中部则不倒装,本句用 which not only improves … but also makes … 不倒装更稳。

Today, government-funded fitness equipment and newly paved fitness trails can be seen everywhere in many cities, which has not only markedly improved the conditions for residents' outdoor activities but also made cities more beautiful.
